Params: {3: 'Before dawn can lift the darkness from the sky, you find your way back to the deck alone.'}
{3: 'The repeater retrofit seems to have reached its end. The two members of the cable-laying crew are gathering up the scattered parts.'}
{3: 'The marine engineer quickly drops his gaze.'}
{1: '1', 3: 'Sensing the delicate atmosphere, a member of the cable-laying team speaks up to lift the mood.'}
{2: 'Sava', 3: 'Gray Raven Commandant, you totally missed out! Larsen was walking us through all these old myths from the Transatlantic coast. It was really interesting.', 4: '2'}
{3: "You came here only to confirm something. One glance at Larsen's evasive eyes tells you everything you need to know."}
{3: 'He is a survivor drowning in guilt, and now he stands before the one child who truly holds the right to judge him.'}
{3: 'That child has not condemned him. And yet her mercy has become a prison from which his guilt will never free him.'}
{3: 'You see no point in pressing the matter.'}
{1: '1', 3: 'Larsen lifts his head, his lips parting slightly. He offers no myths, no distant legends, no entertaining anecdotes.'}
{3: 'He tells the story of a fisherman.'}
{3: 'Of eighty days and more with empty nets. Then the great fish, fought and won. Then the sharks that tore it apart, and the oar that snapped in the struggle.'}
{1: '1', 2: 'Larsen', 3: 'He made it back to the harbor. But the fish was a ruined thing now, just an enormous white skeleton... stretching the whole length of the boat.', 4: '1'}
{3: 'Both cable-laying crew members are fighting to keep their eyes open.'}
{1: '1', 2: 'Sidkosanatrahk', 3: '...So he did all that for nothing?', 4: '2'}
{1: '1', 2: 'Larsen', 3: "Because... that's what this story is about. Failure.", 4: '1'}
{2: 'Larsen', 3: "Perhaps that's simply the truth of it. A person who dares to defy fate... naturally stands closer to ruin than everyone else.", 4: '1'}
{3: "The day's exhaustion sweeps in like the tide, and the deck empties, one person after another, until only you and Larsen remain."}
{2: 'Larsen', 3: "I'm sorry... I... That was the only thing she ever asked of me.", 4: '1'}
{2: "Larsen, you left something out of the fisherman's story.", 3: '59'}
{3: 'It may be true that the person who shakes their fist at a fate that cannot be defied stands closer to ruin than most.'}
{3: 'But being destroyed never means being defeated.'}
{3: 'That is the story most fitting for this ocean, and for mankind.'}
{3: 'A dim blue light wakes across the central panel of the Current Hydrodynamic Energy System. Data streams cascade and disappear. The current parameters jump and recalculate.'}

{3: 'The characters march in neat, orderly lines, each pulse of logic rewriting the world above. Hidden undertows change course. Warm currents curl into new paths. Walls of wind rise, and the waves stack higher and higher.'}
{1: '1', 2: 'Arius', 3: "...A storm requires a certain patience to brew. I do hope... you won't be late.", 4: '1'}
{3: 'The failure at the southern node has, at the very least, revealed their plan to him.'}
{3: 'On the panel before Arius, a spiral cloud formation turns slowly, an almost perfect echo of the storm from decades ago.'}
{3: 'Time has drawn a full circle here, and he stands at its very center, watching history unfold once more.'}
{1: '1', 2: 'Arius', 3: "And I do hope... you'll find this new friend agreeable.", 4: '1'}
{3: 'The colossal whale reforged from the Red Tide and bones glides through the abyss.'}
{3: 'The creatures of the deep grow restless. The Jormungandr node coils along the Mid-Atlantic Ridge like a vast serpent, its silent, invisible "noise" reverberating in an endless Mobius loop.'}
{3: 'The distance shrinks. The prey draws closer.'}
{3: 'Aboard the cable layer, Karenina stands on the forward deck.'}
{3: 'The sea lies eerily still. Overhead, dark clouds sag so low they nearly brush the mast tops, a heavy lid of silence before the coming storm.'}
{3: 'The next second, the ocean surface ruptures.'}
{3: "The giant whale bursts upward, and Karenina's eyes fly wide. Its jagged, monstrous form tears through the surface, a nightmare of crimson and black."}
{3: 'For one frozen heartbeat, it hangs in the air, suspended before every pair of eyes aboard. Then the creature slams down onto the cable layer with obliterating force.'}
{3: 'A violent tremor runs through the hull. The sound of tearing metal rises from below, shrill and agonizing, the exact sound of a fracture.'}
{3: 'Balance shatters across the deck. The crew crashes down in a tangle of limbs, hands flailing and grasping at whatever might hold them steady.'}
{3: 'You are near the stern, inside the sonar control room.'}
{3: 'The girl steadies herself and locks onto your position. In the next heartbeat, the M.I.N.D. connection snaps into place.'}
{3: 'Then the second blow comes. The whale erupts from a new angle, its colossal form filling every field of view.'}
{3: 'The metal, warped past its breaking point from the first strike, finally gives way. The steel keel tears apart with a sound like the world splitting open.'}
{3: 'The center of the hull drops, and the ship snaps in two.'}
{3: 'The sea pours in through the torn hull. The cabin lights blink, falter, and surrender to the dark.'}
{1: '1', 2: 'Sava', 3: 'Emergency lights!!! Someone get the emergency lights on!!!', 4: '18'}
{3: 'Alarms howl through the ship. Emergency lights sputter to life, their red glow carving hurried, jagged silhouettes out of the dark.'}
{3: 'In that dim, dreadful light, Larsen shakes. So many nights have passed, and still he has never escaped this ship.'}
{1: '1', 2: 'Larsen', 3: 'Everyone... fall back to the engine room at the stern!', 4: '1'}
{2: 'Larsen', 3: 'The power units are all aft. We can... steer by engine thrust. Everyone... move to the stern, now!', 4: '1'}
{3: 'His words from that night come back to you now.'}
{1: '1', 2: 'Larsen', 3: '...A storm hit us... a terrible one. Our ship broke in half...', 4: '1'}
{3: 'Everyone moves as the marine engineer commands, fleeing toward the stern.'}
{3: 'A Construct can cross that distance with ease, and you were stationed near the sonar control room at the stern anyway. The seconds stretch generously before you.'}
{3: 'But Larsen is only a man, soft and unseasoned by any physical training. By the time he makes it halfway across the deck, half of the bow has already sunk deep.'}
{3: 'In the next heartbeat, a towering wall of water crashes over him.'}
{3: 'The wave slams into Larsen and rips him off his feet. He has no time to reach for anything before the sea takes him.'}
{3: 'Karenina looks over her shoulder, and her eyes find yours, lingering for a moment. Then she launches herself into the churning sea.'}
{1: '1', 3: 'Through the lashing wind and rain, Rarana wobbles unsteadily, ready to dive in after her.'}
{2: "I'm on a M.I.N.D. connection with Karenina! I'll keep an eye on her!", 3: '254'}
{3: 'The little potted plant hesitates for a second, then spins around and flies back toward you.'}
{3: 'You shelter Rarana close and descend below deck, racing for the engine room as the watertight doors slam down one after another behind you.'}
{3: 'Inside the engine room, the two cable-laying crew members huddle over the control panel, their hands skidding across buttons and dials in a frantic scramble.'}
{1: '1', 2: 'Sidkosanatrahk', 3: 'Do you know how this thing works?', 4: '1'}
{1: '1', 2: 'Sava', 3: 'Larsen said to keep the power steady and steer by engine thrust.', 4: '2'}
{2: 'Sava', 3: "If I knew the answer, I'd be the marine engineer!!!", 4: '2'}
{3: 'They stare at each other, utterly lost.'}
{2: 'Sidkosanatrahk', 3: 'Gray Raven Commandant, you can swim, right?', 4: '1'}
{3: 'The M.I.N.D. connection carries her sensations with brutal clarity. Salt water surges into her nose and throat, bitter and freezing.'}

{3: 'Karenina stands on her surfboard, the propulsion system roaring at full thrust. Larsen is only human, with no protection against the cold. The sea will leech the warmth from his body in minutes.'}
{3: 'That bookish man with his gentle manner, who sang the old song for the dead, who could never look into her eyes...'}
{3: 'She still has too many questions to ask him.'}
{3: 'In the churning dark sea, finding a single person feels impossible. Karenina crests one wave after another, scanning with everything she has.'}

{3: 'The sea is bitter and freezing, each swell slamming into her as though trying to drag her down into the abyss. And that man, that ordinary human who could barely muster the presence of an engineer, how long can he possibly hold on?'}
{1: '1', 3: 'She scrubs the saltwater from her face and pushes every sensor to its absolute limit.'}
{3: 'Her propulsion system glows, a brilliant flare cutting through the dark ocean.'}
{1: '1', 3: 'Amid the wreckage bobbing in the swells, she finally catches sight of the man she has been searching for.'}
{3: 'The marine engineer lies draped over a floating plank, barely hanging on. His lips are blue, his face ghostly pale, all warmth long since leached away.'}
{3: 'Karenina jumps off her surfboard and heaves Larsen onto it.'}
{3: 'Her eyes sweep the water. The dark sky and darker sea squeeze in like a crushing void.'}
{3: 'The battered stern, still tossing on the waves, is nearly out of sight.'}
{3: 'Karenina quickly assesses the situation in her mind.'}
{2: 'Karenina', 3: "(Larsen's body mass, water resistance in storm conditions, my frame's weight...)", 4: '1'}
{2: 'Karenina', 3: '(Would it kill them not to limit my energy output...?!)', 4: '1'}
{3: 'A soundless complaint slips through clenched teeth.'}
{3: 'Her weapon was never built for towing, and with her current load limit, she cannot carry both herself and Larsen back to the remaining half of the ship in time.'}
{1: '1', 2: 'Karenina', 3: "Commandant, I'm granting you control of my weapon.", 4: '1'}
{2: 'Karenina', 3: "Activate the recovery system on the ship. My anchor will track your signal. I'm sending Larsen back first.", 4: '1'}
{3: 'Through the M.I.N.D. connection, you feel every drop of rain lashing against her face.'}
{3: 'You feel her swiping roughly at her face.'}
{2: 'Karenina', 3: "Once he's safe, send the anchor back to me.", 4: '1'}
{3: 'Come what may, Karenina is always the first to throw herself forward.'}
{1: '1', 3: 'She watches as the anchor carries Larsen back toward the stern, which is almost lost from view. A white trail stretches behind him across the dark sea.'}
{3: 'She turns and stares out at the dark, roiling sea beneath the storm.'}
{3: "Her anchor is now gone. She has nothing to ride the waves but her frame's thrusters, pushing through the waters tainted by the Red Tide."}
{3: 'The whale calls drive deeper into her skull, a blunt, rhythmic pounding that will not stop.'}
{3: "As time passes, the pain gnaws at her frame's stability, and her propulsion output wavers, growing more erratic by the second."}
{3: 'The water is far colder than she expected, the chill bleeding through her frame.'}
{3: 'The deep opens beneath her like a starving beast, its jaws yawning wide, drawing her slowly down into its throat.'}
{3: "A raw, ancient instinct kicks in. It's the same bone-deep dread that seized her distant human ancestors when they sensed a predator crouching in the grass."}
{3: 'A stillness heavier than the sea itself presses in on her from all sides, immense and crushing, as though an entire mountain is tilting toward her.'}
{3: 'A colossal whale hangs suspended before her, its face nearly touching hers.'}
{3: 'Plastic waste, rusted metal skeletons, and masses of fish crammed into every seam, all of it knitted together by some unified, terrible will into the monstrous shape of a whale.'}
{3: 'Its eye sockets gape empty, holding only two flickering glows of dim red light.'}
{3: 'Those two murky light orbs rotate slowly in their cavities and fix upon her.'}
{3: "From somewhere within that monstrous silhouette, Arius' voice leaks forth, viscous and languid, like fat dripping through a wound."}
{2: 'Arius', 3: 'I have come to offer you a choice.', 4: '3'}
{3: 'The last thing the M.I.N.D. connection transmits is a flood of black-red, dense as ink, devouring everything in its path.'}
{1: '1', 3: 'In the engine room, Larsen is on his knees, soaked through and heaving for air.'}
{1: '1', 3: 'The two cable-laying crew members haul him upright, but his hands just hover above the control panel, motionless as a frozen statue.'}
{3: "Larsen's fingers spasm uncontrollably. The old memories flood back like a tide and swallow him whole."}
{3: 'He has never truly escaped that shattered ship.'}
{2: 'Larsen', 3: "I can't... I can't go through it again... Not again.", 4: '1'}
{1: '1', 2: 'Sidkosanatrahk', 3: 'You survived that wreck! You made it out! You just need to—', 4: '18'}
{2: 'Larsen', 3: 'Surviving was the worst thing I ever did!!!', 4: '1'}
{2: 'Larsen', 3: 'I should have gone down with that ship!!! With everyone else!!!!!', 4: '1'}
{3: 'It was an unstoppable doom, where Balder fell, and Odin lunged toward Death in rage...'}
{3: 'Where the script of fate turned to its last page.'}
{3: 'In the end, not a single wish came true. In the end, everything lay in ruins.'}
{3: 'They were nothing but ordinary, unlucky, pathetic failures.'}
{3: 'His hand shakes violently on the control stick, like a leaf caught in the wind.'}
{3: 'The M.I.N.D. connection has carried no response from Karenina for too long now. There is no time left to waste.'}
{3: 'You stride quickly to the control panel.'}
{1: '1', 3: "Larsen's face is a wreck. His eyes stare at nothing, unfocused, and his lips move in a mumble, making sounds that no longer shape themselves into words."}
{3: 'The marine engineer is curled in on himself, back bowed in fear. A raw, broken wail escapes him.'}
{3: 'If he can just keep this ship steady, if he can just hold its heading, then the child out there in the storm-ravaged sea will still have a place to return to.'}
{2: 'Larsen', 3: 'I... What am I supposed to do...', 4: '1'}
{3: 'He finally claws his way back to lucidity, but his hands still tremble violently. Any delicate operation remains beyond his grasp.'}
{2: 'If only those gods of yours could help you stay on your feet...', 3: '534'}
{3: 'You turn and look at that frightened, broken soul.'}
{2: 'Then look at me. Tell me what to do.', 3: '536'}
{3: 'His eyes finally calm, coming to rest on the control panel before him.'}
{2: 'Larsen', 3: 'Where are we... where are we going?', 4: '1'}
{2: "We're turning back. We're going to find her.", 3: '542'}
{3: 'The last sensation Karenina registers is the thread deep inside her M.I.N.D., the one that had been pulling her forward, stretched to its breaking point and then snapping clean.'}
{3: 'Her consciousness begins to drift, a buoy severed from its anchor, lost in an ocean of red.'}
{1: 'Now, she has to face everything alone.', 3: '55'}
{2: 'Now, she has to face everything alone.'}
{1: '1', 2: 'Arius', 3: "Such a tone. It rather lacks grace, don't you think?", 4: '18'}
{2: 'Arius', 3: "I see Kalon's guidance left much to be desired... He never did learn how to raise a child properly, after all.", 4: '18'}
{3: 'Karenina is a speck before the monstrous whale, dwarfed by its impossible bulk. Yet her spirit blazes, undiminished, refusing to yield an inch.'}
{2: 'Karenina', 3: "You piece of ****! If you've got something to say, come out here and say it to my face! Let's settle this like real fighters!"}
{1: '1', 2: 'Arius', 3: 'Tch... Do try to curb that temper of yours.', 4: '18'}

{2: 'Arius', 3: "You should understand that the only reason you are alive at all, the only reason you are standing here speaking to me, is because the Erhorn family's eternal obsession runs through you.", 4: '18'}
{3: "A hand of living metal materializes out of the chaos. It barely tightens, and yet something invisible clamps around Karenina's throat, cutting off her air."}
{3: 'Above her, against the crimson void, a face sharpens into view, vast and looming. He watches her thrash and claw at nothing, the way one might admire a delicate, breakable toy.'}

{2: 'Arius', 3: 'In the years of the Black Death, when all of Europe trembled beneath the scythe, the Erhorn family had already begun its work... seeking a way to free humanity from mortal suffering, to unite every soul within a perfect Mother. No pain. No separation. A singular, eternal whole.'}

{2: 'Arius', 3: "Don't let the word trouble you. It is merely a label, a definition shaped by one particular angle of understanding. Call it the Gnostic Son of Man if you prefer, or the anthropomorphic Kadmon... Humanity's little minds have always excelled at inventing such concepts."}
{2: 'Arius', 3: 'For the longest time, I simply called it "the creation of Adam."'}
{1: 'To create<//profane> life is to tread upon the domain of "gods."', 3: '55'}
{2: 'To create<//profane> life is to tread upon the domain of "gods."'}
{2: 'Arius', 3: 'It shall become the origin of every soul, and the destination to which every soul returns.'}
{3: "Arius' voice drops to a soft, gravelly murmur, the tone of a man recounting something sacred, something to be revered above all else."}

{2: 'Arius', 3: "We spent over a thousand years seeking the path back to Adam... The vessel changed over time: blood, gold, quicksilver, then spinal fluid, cerebrospinal fluid, and now... I heard you've given it a new name. The M.I.N.D."}
{2: 'Arius', 3: 'We each navigate and understand this world differently. No two paths ever quite match.'}
{2: 'Arius', 3: 'So... would you like to see mine?'}
{2: 'Arius', 3: 'The brightest monument on this path, the finest work it has ever produced... Karenina.'}
{3: 'The self-proclaimed god loosens his fingers with casual ease and releases his grip.'}
{3: 'The invisible grip releases her, and Karenina gasps for breath. Still, she refuses to lower her head. She meets his arrogant, cruel inspection with her chin raised, unyielding.'}
{3: "The halved cable layer lurches and rolls through the storm, but with Larsen's help, you gradually bring it steady."}
{1: "Perhaps because you have drifted beyond the Red Tide's densest contamination, the M.I.N.D. connection stirs back to life, faint but unmistakable, and finds Karenina's direction.", 5: '1'}
{1: 'Through the shared vision floods a black-red darkness, thick as ink, a wall without end.'}
{1: 'But now you recognize it for what it is. That wall is a giant whale, so enormous it consumes the entire field of view.'}
{2: "Send the anchor to the frame's position.", 3: '630'}
{3: "With the command confirmed, the anchor launches toward Karenina's position."}
